newsitem.title: UK: IRSG sees bigger natural surplus in 1998.
newsitem.headline: IRSG sees bigger natural surplus in 1998.

text.p: The International Rubber Study Group (IRSG) on Friday forecast the world natural rubber surplus at 110,000 tonnes in calendar 1998, against a 90,000 tonnes surplus in 1997.
The group said at the end of its annual meeting that world total rubber consumption (natural and synthetic) would rise to 16.91 million tonnes in 1998 from 16.42 million in 1997.
The 21-member group said there were enough positive factors to expect an improvement in global demand for rubber this year and in 1998.

World rubber production and consumption were expected to continue to increase in the longer term, due to continued growth in Asia and the Pacific and the recovery of the rubber industry in the former Soviet Union and central and eastern Europe.

The IRSG said natural rubber production will increase to 6.72 million tonnes in 1998 from 6.49 million in 1997, while consumption will increase by four percent to 6.61 million tonnes in the same period
